verdicts.text: The Pulumi for Terraform Users guide teaches how to reference existing Terraform state files from Pulumi, use any Terraform provider in Pulumi programs, import and use Terraform modules directly, convert HCL code to Pulumi, and orchestrate Terraform and Pulumi deployments together (recap of earlier guide pages that should cover each topic).
verdicts.evidence: (escalated from pass3) Each of the five recap topics has its own sibling page under parent `terraform-get-started`: reference-state.md ("Reference Terraform State", w4), terraform-modules.md ("Import Terraform Modules", w5), terraform-providers.md ("Use Terraform Providers", w6), convert-hcl.md ("Convert HCL Code", w7), orchestrate.md ("Orchestrate Together", w8). The list is also word-for-word the same as the "What you'll learn" list in _index.md.

verdicts.text: 5. **Consider migration**: When ready, plan a gradual migration to Pulumi for new projects
verdicts.evidence: This line is advice to the reader ("When ready, plan a gradual migration"), not a factual statement that can be proven true or false. The regex flagged "When ready" as temporal, but the phrase doesn't say anything about recency, a version or a date.

verdicts.text: In the multi-stack example, a core infrastructure stack that 'could be Terraform' is consumed from a Pulumi application stack via `pulumi.StackReference("core-infra")` and `getOutput("vpcId")` (a StackReference reads outputs of a Pulumi stack; the core stack exports `vpc`, not `vpcId`).
verdicts.evidence: The claim describes L47-54 accurately: the "core infrastructure stack (could be Terraform)" has `export const vpc`, and the app stack calls `new pulumi.StackReference("core-infra")` and `getOutput("vpcId")`. The stacks concepts docs back up the note in the claim: "The `StackReference` constructor takes as input a string of the form `<organization>/<project>/<stack>`, and lets you access the outputs of that stack". So a StackReference reads Pulumi stack outputs, not Terraform state, and there is no `vpcId` export for it to read. The example itself is internally inconsistent in two ways ("could be Terraform" and `vpc` vs `vpcId`), and the doc should fix both.
verdicts.intuition_flag: Doc bug in the code sample: a StackReference can't consume a Terraform stack, and the export name `vpc` doesn't match `getOutput("vpcId")`.

verdicts.text: The Pulumi Terraform provider (`@pulumi/terraform`) exposes a `terraform.state.S3Reference` class that takes `bucket` and `key` arguments to reference a Terraform state stored in S3 (the documented resource is typically `terraform.state.RemoteStateReference` with a `backendType` of "s3").
verdicts.evidence: There is no `terraform.state.S3Reference` class in the current @pulumi/terraform Node.js SDK. `sdk/nodejs/state/index.ts` only exports the functions `getAzureRMReference`, `getLocalReference`, `getRemoteReference` and `getS3Reference` (plus their `*Output` variants): "export const getS3Reference: typeof import(\"./getS3Reference\").getS3Reference". That means code like `new terraform.state.S3Reference(...)` and its `.getOutput()` calls won't compile. The docs should use `terraform.state.getS3ReferenceOutput({bucket, key, ...})` instead.
verdicts.intuition_flag: Line 203 also uses `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference`, which is a namespace that doesn't exist. The example code looks made up.

verdicts.text: ### Complex state referencing
verdicts.evidence: The text is a Markdown section heading ("### Complex state referencing"). It makes no falsifiable assertion and has no third-party attribution. The regex picked up the word "Complex" as a source hint by mistake.

verdicts.text: `aws.ecs.Cluster` accepts a `configuration.executeCommandConfiguration` argument with `kmsKeyId` and `logging` properties, where `logging: "DEFAULT"` is a valid value.
verdicts.evidence: The pulumi-aws Python SDK (sdk/python/pulumi_aws/ecs/outputs.py) defines the types 'ClusterConfiguration' and 'ClusterConfigurationExecuteCommandConfiguration'. The upstream bridged Terraform schema documents execute_command_configuration with "`kms_key_id` - (Optional) KMS key ID..." and "`logging` - (Optional) ... Valid values: `NONE`, `DEFAULT`, `OVERRIDE`."
verdicts.framing_note: The upstream fields kms_key_id and logging become kmsKeyId and logging in the Pulumi Node.js SDK, following the bridge's standard camelCase conversion.

verdicts.text: `pulumi import` can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.
verdicts.evidence: The auto-generated CLI reference (taken from pulumi/pulumi source) says: "Resources that are not managed by Pulumi can be imported into a Pulumi stack using this command." It also lists a `--from string` flag that will "Invoke a converter to import the resources", which is how Terraform state gets imported (`--from terraform`).

verdicts.text: State ownership can be transferred from Terraform to Pulumi gradually, resource-by-resource.
verdicts.evidence: Pulumi's official migration guide says you can "Import existing resources into Pulumi in the usual way" (that is, `pulumi import` on one resource at a time) or adopt a whole .tfstate with `pulumi import --from terraform`. It also supports coexistence ("Coexist with resources provisioned by Terraform or CDKTF by referencing a .tfstate file"), so moving resources over one by one is supported. One caveat: a third-party guide (Encore) advises splitting ownership at module or stack boundaries rather than per resource inside a module, and says to run `terraform state rm` on each imported resource.
verdicts.source: https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/guides/migration/migrating-to-pulumi/from-terraform/ (WebSearch ran query "Pulumi migrate from Terraform incrementally import resources state"); https://encore.dev/articles/migrate-terraform-to-pulumi
verdicts.framing_note: The live next-steps page (the file under review) has the same wording; it wasn't used as evidence.

verdicts.text: The command syntax `pulumi import <type-token> <name> <id>` (e.g. `pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345`, `aws:ec2/subnet:Subnet`, and `aws:ecs/cluster:Cluster app-cluster my-cluster`) is valid for importing existing VPC, subnet, and ECS cluster resources.
verdicts.evidence: The auto-generated CLI reference says "If using the command line args directly, the type token, name, id and optional flags must be provided. For example: pulumi import 'aws:iam/user:User' name id", and its JSON example uses the token "aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc". `aws:ec2/subnet:Subnet` and `aws:ecs/cluster:Cluster` are the standard pulumi-aws type tokens; an ECS cluster is imported by its name.
verdicts.framing_note: I did not open the pulumi-aws schema to confirm the subnet and ECS cluster tokens directly; they follow the provider's usual naming pattern.

verdicts.text: Pulumi provides an import API that can be used programmatically within a Pulumi program to import resources.
verdicts.evidence: The resource-option docs confirm you can import resources from inside a Pulumi program: "The `import` resource option imports an existing cloud resource so that Pulumi can manage it". Examples show `{ import: "sg-..." }` in TypeScript, `pulumi.Import(...)` in Go and similar forms in the other SDKs. The claim comes from a placeholder code comment ("// Use Pulumi import API to import resources") with no implementation behind it, and it never names the actual mechanism.
verdicts.intuition_flag: "Import API" is vague: the programmatic mechanisms are the `import` resource option (or Automation API stack import). The stub comment doesn't show how to use either one, so readers may not find it useful.

verdicts.text: Pulumi policies (Policy as Code / `@pulumi/policy` PolicyPack) can implement infrastructure policies that work across both Terraform and Pulumi resources.
verdicts.evidence: The Pulumi Policies docs say: "apply them consistently across resources managed by Pulumi IaC, provisioned with Terraform or CloudFormation, or created manually." Coverage of Terraform resources comes from audit mode, which scans resources found through Insights Discovery. Preventative mode checks only Pulumi stack resources during preview/up.
verdicts.intuition_flag: The claim itself holds, but the code sample next to it is a preventative PolicyPack (validateResourceOfType aws.ec2.Instance). That pack runs only during `pulumi preview`/`up`, so it won't check Terraform-managed resources unless it runs as an audit policy over Insights Discovery. Readers may take the wrong idea from the example.

verdicts.text: `@pulumi/policy` exports `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType`; policies accept `name`, `description`, `enforcementLevel: "mandatory"`, and `validateResource` with a callback signature `(resource, args, reportViolation)`.
verdicts.evidence: The SDK source's own doc example shows `import { PolicyPack, validateResourceOfType } from "@pulumi/policy";` with a policy that sets `name`, `description`, `enforcementLevel: "mandatory"`, and `validateResource: validateResourceOfType(aws.s3.Bucket, (bucket, args, reportViolation) => {...})`. `EnforcementLevel` includes "mandatory". One caveat: the three-argument `(resource, args, reportViolation)` signature belongs to the callback you pass to `validateResourceOfType`. A bare `validateResource` callback takes only `(args, reportViolation)`.
verdicts.framing_note: The 3-arg callback is correct only when wrapped in validateResourceOfType. The raw ResourceValidation type is (args, reportViolation).

verdicts.text: `aws.s3.Bucket` resources expose an `acl` property whose values include "public-read" and "public-read-write".
verdicts.evidence: pulumi-aws sdk/nodejs/s3/bucket.ts defines `acl` on `Bucket`: "Canned ACL to apply. Valid values are `private`, `public-read`, `public-read-write`, `aws-exec-read`, `authenticated-read`, and `log-delivery-write`." The property is marked "@deprecated acl is deprecated. Use the aws.s3.BucketAcl resource instead."
verdicts.framing_note: The claim is accurate, but `acl` is deprecated in favor of aws.s3.BucketAcl. The docs might want to mention that.

verdicts.text: The Pulumi Automation API allows embedding Pulumi in applications for dynamic infrastructure management.
verdicts.evidence: The Automation API README in the Pulumi SDK says it is "the programmatic interface for driving Pulumi programs without the CLI". Its listed use cases include "Building higher level tools, custom CLIs over pulumi" and "Using pulumi behind a REST or GRPC API". Together these support the claim that it lets you embed Pulumi in applications to manage infrastructure dynamically.

verdicts.text: The Pulumi Automation API is imported from `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` and provides `LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack({stackName, projectName, program})`, `stack.setConfig(key, {value})`, `stack.up({onOutput})`, and an `outputs` property on the up result.
verdicts.evidence: The Node.js SDK file sdk/nodejs/automation/localWorkspace.ts defines `static async createOrSelectStack(args: InlineProgramArgs, opts?: LocalWorkspaceOptions): Promise<Stack>`. InlineProgramArgs takes stackName/projectName/program, and the module is exported as `@pulumi/pulumi/automation`. I didn't fetch stack.ts, so `Stack.setConfig(key, ConfigValue{value})`, `up({onOutput})` and `UpResult.outputs` are confirmed only by the file's imports (`ConfigValue` from ./config, `OutputMap, Stack` from ./stack) and known SDK surface, not by a fetched source passage.

verdicts.text: `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference` is accessible from the `pulumi` namespace imported via `import * as pulumi from "@pulumi/pulumi/automation"`.
verdicts.evidence: The `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` entry point (sdk/nodejs/automation/index.ts) only re-exports "./cmd", "./config", "./errors", "./stack", "./stackSettings", "./projectSettings", "./localWorkspace", "./workspace", "./events", "./remoteStack", "./remoteWorkspace" and "./tag". It has no `terraform` namespace, so `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference` doesn't exist on that import. Elsewhere the page imports `terraform` from `@pulumi/terraform` instead, so the L203 snippet contradicts the rest of the page.
verdicts.intuition_flag: Separately, `S3Reference` may not exist in @pulumi/terraform either; its state module exposes `RemoteStateReference`. Worth checking.

verdicts.text: Pulumi component resources can wrap Terraform-managed infrastructure so that developers create components without knowing they depend on Terraform-managed resources, leaving multi-tool complexity to the platform team.
verdicts.evidence: The component docs say components "encapsulate related resources and their configuration, letting consumers create complex infrastructure through a simple, well-defined interface—without needing to know the implementation details." A component can therefore read Terraform state outputs internally (via @pulumi/terraform) and keep that dependency hidden from the developers who use it. I couldn't confirm the exact Terraform state API used in the example because the GitHub search was rate-limited (HTTP 403).
verdicts.framing_note: The general component-encapsulation capability covers the specific case of wrapping Terraform-state-backed infrastructure. The 'platform team' part describes an organizational practice, not a product behavior.
verdicts.intuition_flag: The example at L248 uses `terraform.state.S3Reference`, and I'm not sure @pulumi/terraform exports that type (RemoteStateReference is the known class). Worth checking the code sample separately.

verdicts.text: `pulumi.ComponentResource` subclasses call `super(type, name, {}, opts)` with a type token such as `custom:WebApplication` and use `this.registerOutputs({...})`.
verdicts.evidence: This is the standard `@pulumi/pulumi` ComponentResource pattern. The repo's build-a-component guide says: "we also need to call the base class constructor `super(...)`. The first parameter is the name of the resource type… we pass the `name`, `args`, and `opts` values", and "calling `this.registerOutputs` signals Pulumi that the component creation process has completed." I couldn't read the SDK source because of GitHub rate limits and a raw-fetch error. A local component can use any type string, so `custom:WebApplication` works, although the guide recommends `<package-name>:index:<component-class-name>` for packaged components.
verdicts.intuition_flag: The two-part token `custom:WebApplication` doesn't follow the guide's `<pkg>:index:<Class>` format for packaged components. That's fine for components that live in the same program.
